legend: Score 1 nuclei are very similar in size to the nuclei of benign pre-existing epithelial cells (< 1.5 times the size), and they show minimal pleomorphism, an even chromatin pattern, and nucleoli that are either not visible or very inconspicuous. Score 2 nuclei are larger (1.5–2 times the size of benign epithelial cell nuclei), with mild to moderate pleomorphism and visible but small and inconspicuous nucleoli. Score 3 nuclei are even larger (> 2 times the size of benign epithelial cell nuclei), with vesicular chromatin; they vary markedly in size and shape and often show prominent nucleoli.

Tubules and glandular/acini formation are assessed throughout the whole tumour at low magnification; only structures exhibiting clear central lumina surrounded by polarized neoplastic cells are counted: > 75% tubule formation is assigned a score of 1; 10–75% a score of 2; and < 10% a score of 3.

Lymphovascular invasion in stromal tissue immediately adjacent to an invasive carcinoma. Note the central luminal placement of the tumour cells, surrounding space, and lining of the vessel by endothelial cells.
The tumour shows prominent gland/tubule formation (score 1), some nuclear pleomorphism (score 2), and no visible mitotic figures (score 1). Total score 4 = grade 1.

There is no evidence of gland/tubule formation (score 3). The tumour nuclei are large and pleomorphic (score 3). Numerous mitotic figures are visible, with a frequency in 2 mm<sup>2</sup> indicating a score 3. Total score 9 = grade 3.
Inactivating mutations in breast cancer include truncating deletion, missense, and splice site mutations.

Result category

Criteria

Clinical implications

Negative (score 0 / absent membrane staining)a

No staining observed

HER2 null (not currently eligible for trastuzumab deruxtecan in the metastatic setting)

Negative (score 0+ / with membrane staining)a

Membrane staining that is incomplete and is faint / barely perceptible and within ≤ 10% of tumour cells

HER2 ultralow as defined by DB-06 and may be eligible for trastuzumab deruxtecan in the metastatic setting

Negative (score 1+)a

Incomplete membrane staining that is faint / barely perceptible and within > 10% of tumour cells

HER2 low as defined by DB-04/06 and may be eligible for trastuzumab deruxtecan in the metastatic setting

Equivocal (score 2+)a,c

Weak to moderate complete membrane staining in > 10% of tumour cells

or

Complete membrane staining that is intense but within ≤ 10% of tumour cellsb

HER2 low if not amplified by in situ hybridization as defined by DB-04/06 and may be eligible for trastuzumab deruxtecan in the metastatic setting

HER2-positive if amplified and eligible for a variety of HER2-targeted therapies

Positive (score 3+)

Complete membrane staining that is intense and in > 10% of tumour cellsb

Note: If clustered heterogeneity is present, report the % with 3+ staining and the staining in non-expressed populations

HER2-positive and eligible for a variety of HER2-targeted therapies

DB, Destiny Breast.

aAn optional standardized reporting comment for HER2 0, 0+, 1+, or 2+ immunohistochemistry results can be included as follows: “In the Destiny Breast 04 and 06 trials, ‘HER2 low’ was considered immunohistochemistry score 1+ or 2+ / in situ hybridization–negative, and ‘HER2 ultralow’ was considered immunohistochemistry score 0 (pattern 0+) with membrane staining that is incomplete and faint / barely perceptible in ≤ 10% of tumour cells. Breast cancers with these staining patterns may be eligible for treatment with trastuzumab deruxtecan in the metastatic setting (but those with no staining, immunohistochemistry 0, are currently excluded).” bReadily appreciated using a low-power objective and observed within a homogeneous and contiguous population of invasive tumour cells. cAdditional less-common staining patterns, such as moderate to intense but incomplete membrane staining (basolateral staining often seen in micropapillary cancers), are also categorized as score 2+. Equivocal 2+ results should reflex to testing to determine final HER2 status (same specimen using in situ hybridization), or order a new test (new specimen if available, using immunohistochemistry or in situ hybridization).

Kimberly H. Allison
Pathology

Stanford
tablehtml:
ER result category

Criteria

Comments

Positive

≥ 10% of tumour cell nuclei are immunoreactive

Include in the report the overall per cent of cancer cells staining as a range or specific number.

Intensity of staining is reported semi-quantitatively as an average (1+, 2+, or 3+).

Low positive

1–10% of tumour cell nuclei are immunoreactive

The following report comment is recommended and is available to add in standardized form in the “Comments on ER results” section:

·       “The cancer in this sample has a low level (1–10%) of ER expression by immunohistochemistry. There are limited data on the overall benefit of endocrine therapies for patients with low-level (1–10%) ER expression, but they currently suggest possible benefit, so patients are considered eligible for endocrine treatment. There are data that suggest that invasive cancers with these results are heterogeneous in both behaviour and biology and often have gene expression profiles more similar to ER-negative cancers.”

The low-positive designation applies only to invasive carcinoma and is not required for PR or ductal carcinoma in situ.

Include the status of internal controls in the report.

If internal controls are absent but external controls stain appropriately, include the recommended comment:

·       “No internal controls are present, but external controls are appropriately positive. If needed, testing another specimen that contains internal controls may be warranted for confirmation of ER status.”

Negative

< 1% of tumour cell nuclei are immunoreactive

Include the status of internal controls in the report.

If internal controls are absent but external controls stain appropriately, include the recommended comment:

·       “No internal controls are present, but external controls are appropriately positive. If needed, testing another specimen that contains internal controls may be warranted for confirmation of ER status.”

title: Table 3.06 Assays validated for clinical decision-making in early-stage breast cancer
tablehtml:
Assay

Validated use

21-gene recurrence score

Predicts the benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy and risk of distant recurrence in ER+/ERBB2 (HER2)−, node-negative, or limited node-positive (1–3 nodes) early-stage breast cancer

70-gene signature

Estimates the risk of distant recurrence in ER+/HER2−, node-negative, or limited node-positive (1–3 nodes) early breast cancer (used in decision to withhold chemotherapy)

EPclin

Predicts the risk of distant recurrence and added value of chemotherapy in ER+/HER2− early breast cancer (node-negative or 1–3 nodes)

PAM50

Intrinsic subtype classification and estimates the risk of distant recurrence for postmenopause ER+/HER2−, node-negative, or limited node-positive early breast cancer

Breast Cancer Index

Predicts the benefit from extended endocrine therapy (5–10 years) in ER+/HER2− early breast cancer
